tips.title: Try Meatless Mondays
tips.description: Replacing meat with plant-based meals just one day a week can save approximately 0.6 kg CO₂e per meal. Over a year, that's over 30 kg of emissions avoided.

tips.title: Buy Local & Seasonal Produce
tips.description: Locally grown, seasonal fruits and vegetables travel shorter distances and require less refrigeration. This can reduce food-related emissions by up to 10%.

tips.title: Reduce Food Waste
tips.description: Plan your meals, store food properly, and use leftovers creatively. About 1/3 of all food produced globally is wasted, contributing 8-10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.

tips.title: Choose Plant-Based Milk
tips.description: Switching from dairy milk to oat or soy milk can reduce emissions by up to 70%. One glass of dairy milk produces about 0.6 kg CO₂e vs 0.2 kg for plant-based alternatives.

tips.title: Grow Your Own Herbs
tips.description: Growing herbs at home (tulsi, mint, coriander) eliminates packaging and transport emissions. It also reduces plastic waste from store-bought herbs.

tips.title: Carry a Reusable Water Bottle
tips.description: Manufacturing a single plastic bottle produces about 82.8g of CO₂. Using a reusable bottle for a year saves approximately 30 kg CO₂ and prevents 150+ plastic bottles from entering waste streams.

tips.title: Reduce Processed Food Intake
tips.description: Processed and packaged foods have 2-3x the carbon footprint of whole foods due to manufacturing, packaging, and cold-chain logistics.

tips.title: Start Composting Kitchen Waste
tips.description: Composting organic waste instead of sending it to landfill prevents methane emissions (25x more potent than CO₂). Even a small kitchen compost bin makes a difference.

tips.title: Use Public Transport
tips.description: Taking a bus emits 50-75% less CO₂ per passenger-km than driving alone. Metro/trains are even better, producing about 80% less emissions than a car.

tips.title: Cycle for Short Trips
tips.description: For trips under 5 km, cycling is zero-emission and saves approximately 0.19 kg CO₂ per km compared to a petrol car. Plus, it's great exercise!

tips.title: Carpool to Work or College
tips.description: Sharing a car ride with 3 others reduces per-person emissions by 75%. Many apps now make carpooling easy and affordable.

tips.title: Work/Study from Home When Possible
tips.description: Each day of remote work eliminates your commute emissions entirely. Even 2 days/week of WFH can save 200+ kg CO₂ per year.

tips.title: Maintain Your Vehicle Properly
tips.description: Properly inflated tires, regular servicing, and removing unnecessary weight can improve fuel efficiency by 3-5%, saving both emissions and money.

tips.title: Choose Train Over Flight for Short Trips
tips.description: A domestic flight emits about 6x more CO₂ per km than a train journey. For distances under 500 km, trains are both greener and often more convenient.

tips.title: Walk for Very Short Distances
tips.description: For trips under 2 km, walking is the most sustainable option. It produces zero emissions and improves your health. Many short car trips can easily be walked.

tips.title: Switch to LED Bulbs
tips.description: LED bulbs use 75% less energy than incandescent bulbs and last 25x longer. Replacing 10 bulbs in your home can save over 100 kg CO₂ per year.

tips.title: Unplug Devices When Not in Use
tips.description: Standby power (phantom load) accounts for 5-10% of home electricity use. Unplugging chargers, TVs, and appliances when not in use can save 50+ kg CO₂/year.

tips.title: Use a Fan Instead of AC
tips.description: A ceiling fan uses about 75W vs 1500W+ for an AC. Even using a fan for 4 hours instead of AC daily can save over 400 kg CO₂ per year.

tips.title: Set AC to 24°C or Higher
tips.description: Every degree below 24°C increases AC energy consumption by 6-8%. Setting your AC to 24°C instead of 20°C can save 25-30% on cooling energy.

tips.title: Use Solar Water Heater
tips.description: A solar water heater can reduce your water heating energy by 70-80%. In sunny regions of India, it's one of the best investments for reducing emissions.

tips.title: Wash Clothes in Cold Water
tips.description: About 90% of energy used by washing machines goes to heating water. Washing in cold water can reduce laundry emissions by 50% with no loss in cleaning quality.

tips.title: Air Dry Your Clothes
tips.description: Using a clothesline instead of an electric dryer saves about 2.4 kg CO₂ per load. India's climate makes air drying practical for most of the year.

tips.title: Use a Pressure Cooker
tips.description: Pressure cookers use 70% less energy than conventional cooking methods. They cook food faster, saving both time and gas/electricity.

tips.title: Buy Less, Choose Well
tips.description: The fashion industry produces 10% of global carbon emissions. Buying fewer, higher-quality items that last longer significantly reduces your fashion footprint.

tips.title: Choose Second-Hand or Thrift
tips.description: Buying second-hand extends product life and avoids the emissions from manufacturing new items. Each second-hand garment saves approximately 5-10 kg CO₂.

tips.title: Carry Reusable Bags
tips.description: India generates 26,000 tonnes of plastic waste daily. Carrying your own cloth/jute bag eliminates the need for single-use plastic bags.

tips.title: Repair Instead of Replace
tips.description: Repairing electronics, clothes, and furniture instead of replacing them avoids manufacturing emissions. A repaired phone saves 70 kg CO₂ vs buying new.

tips.title: Avoid Excessive Online Ordering
tips.description: Each express delivery package generates 3-4x the emissions of standard shipping. Batch your orders and avoid single-item deliveries.

tips.title: Use a Refillable Steel Straw & Cutlery Set
tips.description: Single-use plastic straws and cutlery add up quickly. A reusable set prevents hundreds of plastic items from entering landfills each year.

tips.title: Keep Your Phone Longer
tips.description: Manufacturing a smartphone produces ~70 kg CO₂. Using your phone for 4 years instead of 2 effectively halves its annual carbon impact.

tips.title: Segregate Your Waste
tips.description: Separating wet, dry, and hazardous waste at source enables proper recycling and composting. This can divert 60-80% of waste from landfills.

tips.title: Say No to Single-Use Plastics
tips.description: Refuse plastic straws, cups, plates, and packaging whenever possible. Each kg of plastic avoided prevents 6 kg of CO₂ from being emitted during production.

tips.title: Donate What You Don't Need
tips.description: Instead of throwing away clothes, electronics, or furniture, donate them. This extends their useful life and prevents manufacturing emissions from replacements.

tips.title: Recycle E-Waste Properly
tips.description: E-waste contains toxic materials that pollute soil and water in landfills. Proper e-waste recycling recovers valuable materials and prevents environmental contamination.

tips.title: Use Cloth Napkins & Towels
tips.description: Replacing paper towels and napkins with washable cloth alternatives saves trees and reduces waste. One cloth napkin replaces thousands of paper ones over its lifetime.

tips.title: Fix Leaky Taps Immediately
tips.description: A dripping tap can waste 20+ liters of water per day. Fixing leaks conserves water and reduces the energy needed to treat and pump water.

tips.title: Take Shorter Showers
tips.description: Reducing shower time by 2 minutes saves about 20 liters of water per shower. If using hot water, this also saves significant energy.

tips.title: Harvest Rainwater
tips.description: Rainwater harvesting reduces dependency on groundwater and municipal supply. Collected rainwater can be used for gardening, cleaning, and even filtered for drinking.

tips.title: Use a Bucket Instead of Running Water
tips.description: Using a bucket for bathing, washing dishes, or cleaning uses 60-70% less water than running a tap or shower continuously.

tips.title: Avoid Bottled Beverages
tips.description: Manufacturing and transporting bottled drinks is highly carbon-intensive. Opt for homemade juices, filtered water, and tap alternatives to cut emissions.

tips.title: Use Natural Light During the Day
tips.description: Open curtains and blinds to maximize daylight instead of switching on lights. Proper window placement and light-colored walls can reduce lighting energy by 50%.

tips.title: Use 5-Star Rated Appliances
tips.description: BEE 5-star rated appliances consume 30-50% less energy than lower-rated ones. When buying new appliances, always check the energy rating label.

tips.title: Consider an Electric Two-Wheeler
tips.description: Electric scooters produce 0 direct emissions and cost only ₹15-20 to charge fully. They're ideal for daily commutes under 80 km.

tips.title: Choose Products with Minimal Packaging
tips.description: Excess packaging contributes significantly to waste. Prefer products with recyclable or minimal packaging, and buy in bulk when possible.

tips.title: Make Your Own Cleaning Products
tips.description: DIY cleaning solutions using vinegar, baking soda, and lemon are effective, cheap, and eliminate plastic packaging from commercial cleaners.

tips.title: Plant Trees Around Your Home
tips.description: Trees provide natural cooling, reducing AC needs by up to 25%. A single mature tree absorbs about 22 kg of CO₂ per year.

tips.title: Use Reusable Containers for Takeaway
tips.description: Carry your own steel or glass containers when ordering takeaway food. This eliminates disposable plastic and styrofoam containers.

tips.title: Go Paperless
tips.description: Switch to digital documents, e-bills, and online submissions. Each kg of paper saved prevents approximately 1.5 kg of CO₂ emissions from production.

tips.title: Use a Ride-Sharing App Efficiently
tips.description: When using cab services, opt for shared/pool rides instead of solo rides. This can reduce per-trip emissions by 30-50%.

tips.title: Install Low-Flow Fixtures
tips.description: Low-flow showerheads and tap aerators reduce water flow by 40-60% without noticeably affecting pressure, saving both water and heating energy.
